steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An interest rate is the cost of borrowing or the reward for saving, expressed as a percentage of the amount.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Higher interest rates: encourage saving (better returns), discourage borrowing (more expensive loans), reduce spending (mortgages cost more, less disposable income), and reduce business investment (borrowing costs rise).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Lower interest rates: discourage saving, encourage borrowing and spending, stimulate investment, and can lead to inflation if demand grows too fast.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Bank of England sets the base interest rate to control inflation — raising rates to cool the economy, lowering to stimulate it.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how a rise in interest rates affects consumers' decisions to save, borrow, and spend. | Explain how a fall in interest rates might affect a firm's decision to invest in new equipment. | Evaluate whether the Bank of England should raise interest rates when inflation is rising.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link interest rate changes to BOTH consumers AND producers in your answer. The Bank of England targets 2% CPI inflation — this is the key context for interest rate decisions. Real interest rate = nominal rate - inflation rate. This matters because high inflation erodes the real value of savings.
